report_limits: New captures use two guard iterations on each side and fixed sample IDs linked to caller-stream device events. Guards and event markers are excluded from kernel timing. Missing measured stages remain errors. Legacy captures retain strict whole-window validation.

official_logical_bytes follows the DeepEP-Ascend test numerator: all rank-deduplicated receive rows including self; dispatch/cached use x+scales+full top-k indices/weights, combine uses BF16 x only. This is logical accounting, not actual wire bytes. Matching the numerator does not match timing boundaries.

Remote application bytes exclude self, count rank-deduplicated payload and actual field writes. They are not NIC/wire bytes: packet headers, ACK/retries and SHMEM collective control traffic are unmeasured.
comm_us is the complete communication kernel, including local work, synchronization, metadata and (dispatch) GM output copy; it is not an isolated NIC transfer timer.
device_sum_us sums all API device kernels. device_span_us includes gaps between those kernels; caller_us is measured separately without profiler and includes host submission/event waits.
combine_stage_us = aggregate_us + comm_us; excludes notify and final reduce. It is reported separately from comm_us and full API time.

For early single-source combine, comm_us is early_submit_us + late_comm_us. The NIC can progress during aggregate; comm_us alone is not the full transfer interval. Use combine_stage_us for aggregate plus communication, or combine_stage_span_us including kernel gaps.
Algorithm bytes = T*K*H*element_bytes, including invalid top-k slots. valid_algorithm_bytes excludes invalid slots. Combine payload is always BF16.

L2 eviction mode is recorded in flush_l2_cache/l2_flush_bytes. When enabled, eviction precedes each full API call and is excluded from all API timing fields; internal stages are not flushed. This is cache eviction by memory writes, not a hardware invalidation guarantee. Repeated fixed routing/input, caller allocation, independent GM outputs. A bandwidth comparison also requires matching routing, caching, hardware and library versions.
